stories.headline: Why crocodiles outlived the dinosaurs
stories.summary: A UCL-led team studied 400+ species across 245 million years. Crocodiles always followed warm climates, which kept survivors in tropical refuges that stayed livable after the asteroid hit.
stories.why: It helps solve a 66-million-year-old mystery, and shows today's crocodiles need room to move as the planet warms.

stories.headline: Four new frog species found in Peru
stories.summary: Biologists used body traits, mating calls and DNA to describe four new Oreobates frogs near Cordillera Azul National Park, taking the group from 27 to 31 known species.
stories.why: Naming a species is the first step to protecting it, and frogs can help justify protected areas.

stories.stat_label: years of work to reach the sky
stories.headline: A glass chip made two telescopes work as one
stories.summary: A palm-sized chip from Heriot-Watt University combined starlight from two CHARA telescopes, a job that usually needs bulky mirrors and lenses. It even picked up fainter stars than the old system.
stories.why: Smaller, swappable chips could help astronomers study planets around other stars.

stories.stat_label: since Hokkaido's last harvest this good
stories.headline: Japan's potato island had its best harvest in a decade
stories.summary: A cooler summer with steady rain gave Hokkaido, which grows 80% of Japan's potatoes, denser, rounder spuds while heat hit crops across much of the Northern Hemisphere.
stories.why: Calbee expects to get back to its usual 250,000 tons of Hokkaido potatoes.

fun_fact: About 50 million years ago, crocodile relatives lived as far south as Antarctica.
